issues.description: Method addGuestStudents(int) has conflicting return types: the problem statement's UML declares addGuestStudents(int): void (problem_statement.md line 73) and the textual task describes adding guest students without specifying a return (problem_statement.md line 50), but the reference solution implements public boolean addGuestStudents(int) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 90). This mismatch can confuse students about the required method signature and expected behavior (should the method return a boolean success flag or be void?), and may cause graders/tests or example code to disagree with a student's implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addGuestStudents(int) signature consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred if exercise intends no return): change the solution method to 'public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents)' and update its body to update numberOfGuestStudents without returning a value; update the solution file and ensure the template's TODO and any example code reflect the void signature. Option B (preferred if a success flag is useful): update the UML and problem statement to document and show 'addGuestStudents(int): boolean', explaining the meaning of the boolean return value (e.g., false for negative input), and update the template to declare the method returning boolean. Apply the chosen change to all three places (problem statement UML, template stub, and solution) so students see a single, unambiguous expected signature.
